## Historical audit — S0338

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_v3/results/H04/test/bw_0005/2/trajectory.jsonl`. Citations below refer to its JSONL lines; observations were not split across chunks.

**Goal versus interpretation.** The assigned goal was to reconstruct the visible indoor scene and match the reference camera, framing, objects and materials. The student interpreted the image as a classroom photograph inset within a larger graphic; that interpretation and its changing inset bounds are not independently verified here (H request, line 1; H responses, lines 3 and 23).

| Evidence | Observed operations and results |
|---|---|
| Initial build | H emitted architecture, six framed windows, multiple cabinets, two tables, stools, trays, blocks and a rug. Cabinets and furniture have named component meshes; their hierarchy does not prove physical connection or reference fidelity. Colors and plank-seam geometry approximate materials; no image textures are used. The program sets camera pose, world and two lights (lines 3–4). |
| First validation | Build and render completed, and step 1 was selected (lines 6, 8–10). H then reported an exterior wall occluding the layout and a small cabinet, proposing a closer camera and local changes. These are H’s visual assessments, not independent inspection (lines 11, 13). |
| Second build | H changed camera position, aim and lens, enlarged and repositioned the foreground cabinet, and retained the right wall despite stating an intention to omit the blocking wall (lines 13–14). Execution succeeded. A higher-aim trial moved computed landmark projections downward and was restored; it did not establish the correctness of the major camera change or visibility (lines 19–20). |
| Third build | H reported gray exterior wedges, a cropped rug, pale cabinet recesses and excessive windows in step 2. It expanded the room, moved the cabinet, changed camera pose, reduced six windows to four, darkened colors and lowered lighting; a distant right wall remained. It compared previous and selected cameras on revised geometry and restored a small aim trial (lines 23–24, 29). |
| Final outcome | Step 3 built and rendered successfully and was selected (lines 26, 28–30). Its selected-camera rug landmark projected to y=1.048 against an estimated reference y=0.96; the window and cabinet landmarks also retained substantial differences. These projections are not contour or visibility checks (line 29). No subsequent image review or formal correctness score is visible. |

**Teacher input and autonomy.** No separate teacher event or teacher diagnosis appears in this student trajectory. The actual follow-up inputs were runner-provided results, reference/render images and generic comparison instructions (lines 11 and 21). H’s subsequent diagnoses and revised programs demonstrate response to those inputs, not adoption of a specific teacher-proposed fix. Its sessions recorded no direct tool calls; the external runner executed the three programs (lines 2, 12, 22; execution lines 4, 14, 24).

**Assessment and uncertainty.** This is a technical execution success, with reconstruction correctness **unknown**: no empty patch, algorithm crash or technical interruption is shown, but successful rendering is not geometric or visual verification. The reference and final images themselves are not visible in this audit, so actual object count, part contacts, pose, texture fidelity, lighting and final crop cannot be independently assessed. Whether the inset-only framing was appropriate remains unresolved. Transferably, separate landmark projections from visible contours and compare camera changes on consistent geometry; task-specific window counts and cabinet placement remain hypotheses rather than reusable rules.
